sources.entry: Openfire - Real time collaboration (RTC) server. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Java

summary.one_liner: Openfire is a real-time collaboration (RTC) server built on the XMPP (Jabber) instant messaging protocol, licensed under Apache-2.0.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Openfire as an XMPP server and real-time collaboration (RTC) server under the Apache License, and as an Ignite Realtime community project. It says the server is easy to set up and administer. It has an admin interface whose translations are managed in an i18n folder. The project is built with Maven, with a core module in xmppserver, a distribution module, and a plugins directory for optional plugins. The README gives instructions for building the project and running it from the command line or from IntelliJ IDEA, including a debug mode. The README does not list specific messaging features beyond XMPP support.
use_cases: Running a self-hosted instant messaging server
Hosting an XMPP/Jabber server for a team or organization
Developing or modifying the Openfire XMPP server core
notable: Built on XMPP (Jabber), an open standard instant messaging protocol
Includes a plugin system with plugins built from a separate plugins directory
Maven project that imports into Java IDEs
Part of the Ignite Realtime open source community
caveats: README says Openfire cannot be run from within most IDEs; it must be started from the command line after a Maven build
Bug reports require a Discourse account and access is limited to some users per the README
Several README resource links (documentation, community, bug tracker, nightly builds, translations) are empty in the text provided
keywords: host private chat for my team
